# Orzhov Vampires

- **Format:** Casual 60-card, 1v1
- **Archetype:** Orzhov lifegain-drain midrange: gain life on every creature, grow Pridemates, drain on every trade, and remove the opponent's key threats; a slower grind
- **Played by:** either — suits whoever likes careful decisions, removal and watching life totals swing
- **Status:** idea
- **Paired against:** [Selesnya Rabbits](selesnya-rabbits.md)
- **Complexity:** 3/5
- **Estimated power:** 5.5 with owned cards only, 6.5 with the buys (on a 1v1 scale)
- **Configuration:** Pair 3. It uses no precon cards, so its cards have all arrived and it can be built now, alongside Izzet and Gruul. It's in the **Commander-season** set too (with Giada, Gisa, Izzet and Gruul), where it takes over from Angels vs Zombies once the precons go back to being Commander decks.

A white-black life-gain and drain deck. Small creatures gain you life, Ajani's Pridemates grow every time you do, and Vampires like Vengeful Bloodwitch and Marauding Blight-Priest make the opponent lose life whenever your creatures die or you gain life. It plays slower than the Rabbits: kill their best creatures, trade off the rest, and let the drains, the flyers and Exsanguinate finish. It suits whoever likes careful decisions and watching life totals swing.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **2x Vampire of the Dire Moon** (replaces Vampire Neonate + Kalastria Highborn). 1-mana 1/1 with deathtouch and lifelink. It blocks and kills anything (even a pumped Overrun attacker), and every hit triggers Pridemate and Blight-Priest. About +2.7 pts per copy in the simulator. *Also useful in: any black deck (Gisa, a Mono-B build).*
2. **2x Gifted Aetherborn** (replaces Sun-Blessed Healer + Vampire Spawn). 2-mana 2/3 with deathtouch and lifelink, the best 2-drop against go-wide decks. Walls tokens and fuels the life-gain engine. About +2.4 pts per copy. *Also useful in: any black deck (Gisa, Mono-B Midrange).*
3. **2x Isolated Chapel** (replaces Temple of Silence + Orzhov Guildgate). W/B land that enters untapped once you have a Plains or Swamp, replacing two tapped lands. Reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices, so there's no need to wait. Simpler for beginners than the painland Caves of Koilos. *Also useful in: any W/B deck (Orzhov Removal).*
4. **1x Vampire Nighthawk** (replaces 1 Fiendish Panda). 2nd copy of a flying, deathtouch, lifelink 3-drop, the deck's best card. The cheapest buy of the lot. About +1.7 pts. *Also useful in: any black deck; a Commander staple.*

Ayli, Eternal Pilgrim, Duress, Go for the Throat, Hero's Downfall, Inspiring Overseer, Knight of Malice, Lyra Dawnbringer, Mortify, Night's Whisper, Orzhov Guildgate, Scoured Barrens, Temple of Silence, Tribute to Hunger, Vampire Nighthawk.

| Target-list buy | Owned card played until it arrives | What the swap costs |

| Vampire of the Dire Moon ×2 | Vampire Neonate, Kalastria Highborn | Medium. Neonate is a good wall that pings for 1, and Kalastria drains 2 when a Vampire dies if you keep {B} open, but neither kills attackers. About −2.5 pts per copy |
| Gifted Aetherborn ×2 | Sun-Blessed Healer, Vampire Spawn | Medium. Healer (3/1 lifelink, kicker returns a 2-drop) and Spawn (drain 2) are fine, but neither holds off tokens. About −2 pts per copy |
| Isolated Chapel ×2 | Temple of Silence, Orzhov Guildgate | Two more tapped lands slow the early turns. About −1 to −3 pts |
| Vampire Nighthawk (2nd) | Fiendish Panda (2nd) | Small. Panda grows with life gain and brings back a creature when it dies. About −1.5 pts |

Together the owned list is about 7–9 pts weaker than the target list against the same opponent. That's why the buys should arrive together with the Rabbits' buys.

## Notes

### Game plan
- **Set up the life-gain engine first.** Hinterland Sanctifier and Dazzling Angel gain you 1 life whenever another creature of yours enters.
- **Every life gain** puts a +1/+1 counter on Ajani's Pridemate, Fiendish Panda and Twinblade Paladin. With Marauding Blight-Priest out, it also makes the opponent lose 1. That's the *drain*: they lose life and you gain it.
- **Trade creatures freely.** With Vengeful Bloodwitch out, each of your creatures that dies drains them 1. In the owned list, Kalastria Highborn drains 2 more when a Vampire dies, if you pay {B}.
- **Use removal on their key cards,** block well, and win slowly with flyers (Nighthawk, Overseer, Dazzling Angel, Collector), big Pridemates and Exsanguinate.

### Opening hand and mulligan
- **Keep:** 2–4 lands (3 is ideal) with both colours or an Evolving Wilds, plus an early play (Sanctifier, Pridemate, Bloodwitch) or a removal spell.
- **Mulligan** (shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken): 0–1 lands, 6 or more lands, or a hand whose lands are all one colour while its spells are all the other.

### Play tips
1. **Order matters.** Play Sanctifier or Dazzling Angel before your other creatures, and Pridemate before the life gain happens.
2. **Save the big removal** (Go for the Throat, Hero's Downfall, Mortify) for their key creatures: the ones that pump the whole team (Wilt-Leaf Liege, Valley Questcaller, Regal Caracal, Finneas) and the ones that get huge or draw cards (Burrowguard Mentor, Druid of the Spade, Mentor of the Meek, Harvestrite Host). Moment of Craving is fine on a token.
3. **Respect Overrun.** When they have 5 or more creatures and 5 lands, keep blockers home and your life total high.
4. **Vampire Neonate** (owned list): at the end of their turn, if you have 2 spare mana, tap it to drain 1.
5. **Exsanguinate:** X is your lands minus 2. Cast it as the finisher, or whenever X is 5 or more.
6. **Ayli:** pay {1} and sacrifice a creature that's about to die anyway to gain life equal to its toughness. Bloodwitch still triggers. Once you have 30 or more life, her second ability ({1}{W}{B}, sacrifice another creature) exiles any nonland permanent, so a long game gives you extra removal.

### Watch out for (Rabbits)
- **Overrun** (5 mana, sorcery): all their creatures get +3/+3 and *trample* (damage beyond what kills a blocker goes through). It's their big turn.
- **Rabbit Response** (4 mana, instant): +2/+1 to their team during combat. Don't make blocks that only work if they have no trick.
- **Wilt-Leaf Liege:** +1/+1 to their white creatures and +1/+1 to their green ones (so +2/+2 to green-white creatures). Your top removal target.
- **Burrowguard Mentor** (and Crusader of Odric in their owned list) is as big as their creature count.
- **Warren Elder** (and Dawnwing Marshal in their owned list) pumps the whole team with spare mana.
- **Valley Questcaller** (target list) gives their other Rabbits, tokens included, +1/+1.
- **Broken Wings** kills your flyers. **Bite Down, Rabid Bite and Felling Blow** let their biggest creature kill one of yours.

### Sideboard: vs stronger opponents
Not for games against the Rabbits, because these cards would tip the pair.
- **vs spell-heavy decks** (few creatures): +2 Duress; −2 Moment of Craving.
- **vs go-wide token decks:** +1 Seeker's Folly (−1/−1 to all their creatures); −1 Kalastria Highborn.
- **vs white decks:** +1 Knight of Malice (white removal can't target it); −1 Vampire Spawn.
- **vs slow decks, or just to power up:** +1 Lyra Dawnbringer; −1 Sun-Blessed Healer.
- **vs hexproof or one huge creature:** +1 Tribute to Hunger, +1 Pacifism; −1 Moment of Craving, −1 Fiendish Panda.
- With the target list (no Kalastria Highborn, Vampire Spawn or Sun-Blessed Healer), take out Twinblade Paladin or Bloodtithe Collector instead.

### Head-to-head vs Selesnya Rabbits (tested)

**Verdict: even**, about 51/49 Rabbits with both the owned lists and the lists with buys.

| Rabbits win % | Original simulator | Re-checked simulator |
|---|---|---|
| Owned vs owned | 50–51% | 52% |
| Both with buys | 51% | 51–52% |
| Rabbits with buys, Vampires owned | 60% | 60% |
| Rabbits owned, Vampires with buys | 42% | 45% |

**How it was tested.** A rules simulator played 8,000–10,000 games per matchup, alternating who goes first. An independent re-check reproduced the original results, then fixed six bugs and re-ran them. For example, both Harvestrite Hosts had shared one draw counter, and the attack AI undervalued going wide. What the simulator still leaves out roughly cancels: it has no double blocks and never casts Overrun unless it's lethal, which understates Rabbits, and it gives Vampires no instant-speed removal. Ten simulator games were also reviewed turn by turn (5–5), and 6 more were played by hand (3–3).

**Going first** wins about 53–54% of games.

#### Why it's even
- It's speed against staying power. Rabbits is faster and wider: it kills an empty board around turn 6, Vampires around turn 6.5. Vampires has more life, deathtouch blockers and reach (flyers and Exsanguinate).
- Rabbits has 5 removal spells (bite spells and Broken Wings, which need its own creatures). Vampires has 7.
- No single card is worth more than about 3 points, and neither main deck has a hoser or a one-sided sweeper.
- **Rabbits win** when Burrowguard Mentor or Druid of the Spade gets big alongside Treeguard Duo or an anthem before the removal lines up. **Vampires win** when Rabbits stumble on lands or colours, or when the Hinterland Sanctifier + Pridemate / Blight-Priest engine lands with removal behind it.

#### Buying rule
Each deck's buys are worth about 7–10 points, and upgrading only one deck tips the pair to 55–60%. Upgrade both together, in matched steps: Valley Questcallers with Vampire of the Dire Moons, Sunpetal Groves with Isolated Chapels, then Burrowguard Mentor, Harvestrite Hosts and Hop to It with Gifted Aetherborns and Vampire Nighthawk. On 2026-09-28 MTGMate had no Vampire of the Dire Moon, so hold the Questcallers until the Dire Moons are found. Keep both decks on their owned lists until both packages are complete, then swap them in on the same day.

#### Tuning levers (original simulator estimates)
- **If Rabbits win too often:** Rabbits' Regal Caracal → Pileated Provisioner (about −2), or, with the owned lists, Vampires' Kalastria Highborn → Pacifism or Knight of Malice from its sideboard (about +1 for Vampires).
- **If Vampires win too often:** Rabbits' Rabid Bite → Swords to Plowshares from its sideboard (about +3), or, with the owned lists, Dryad Militant → Stasis Snare (about +1).
- Keep Fumigate and Day of Judgment (free in the pool) out of both decks, because a one-sided sweeper would swing the pair.
- Tier-2 buys weren't simulated together. Buy them in matched pairs and re-check with a few games.

Simulator code and full game logs from the 2026-09-28 analysis are not kept in the repo.
